messages:
rachel: Heads-up: p99 on host ingress climbed ~15% after yesterday's kernel-affinity rollout. Affects chat-small route (single-frame, ~300B payloads).

observability-bot: alert: host-ingress.p99.chat-small > baseline by 15% at 2026-03-22T09:12:00Z

tomas: saw that. traces point to extra allocation/copy in the pre-parse layer when frames come from kernel-affinity v3. can we dump a small flame?

rachel: pasted flame excerpt:
``
40%  http2/recv -> preparse/ensure_contiguous -> memcpy -> tokenizer
22%  preparse/ensure_contiguous -> kvcache/lookup -> evict_then_lookup
10%  sys/read -> http2/recv_frame
```
seems kernel variant now hands back a non-contiguous iovec-like buffer in some cases -> preparse calls ensure_contiguous which mallocs+copies.

dilip: confirmed in local repro. the kernel-selector changed buffer packing for aligned kernels, probably for SIMD kernel expectations. downside: we break zero-copy path for tiny frames.

tomas: options: (A) reintroduce zero-copy fast-path for single-frag frames by checking a new buffer-stability flag from kernel selector, (B) make preparse assemble in-place but use pooled scratch to avoid malloc churn, (C) change kernel selector to prefer stable-backed buffers for small-request routes.

rachel: I prefer A + C: minimal preparse logic and push correctness to kernel selector for tiny frames. We should add a flag in the selector response: backing_stable=true/false. If true, preparse trusts the pointer for lifecycle of request; if false, it must materialize.

dilip: agreed. also seeing kvcache pressure: our fragment key uses full request nonce + seq which makes lots of unique tiny keys and causes churn. We should normalize tiny-fragment keys to just client_prefix+route so identical small requests hit the same shard.

tomas: wrote a quick sim: consolidating keys reduces eviction rate by ~60% in the sim for 10k tiny-reqs.

rachel: nice—combine the two fixes. also tweak batching: current micro-batcher waits 4ms to aggregate, but when frames are tiny that wait causes extra buffering and copy overhead. For small routes set batch_wait=1ms or immediate dispatch.

dilip: microbench results on my laptop after applying backing_stable flag and key normalization: p99 -10%, total heap allocs -38%, kvcache hitrate +22% for tiny cohort.

tomas: pushed a draft PR with the selector flag and preparse fast-path: https://git.internal/r/12567 (WIP). includes small http2 harness script and perf microbench.

rachel: please add unit tests that assert: (1) backing_stable=false leads to materialize path, (2) backing_stable=true avoids allocation and retains stable pointer across lifecycle. Also add integration canary test for chat-small route.

tomas: tests added. also added telemetry tag kernel_affinity=stable_backing_toggle so we can slice dashboards.

build-bot: ci: PR 12567 tests passed (linux-amd64). integration harness flaky on arm64 (known infra flake).

dilip: after merge plan: roll to 5% for 15m, measure p50/p95/p99, then 25% for 30m, check kvcache eviction rate and allocator rate. If p99 regresses >3% revert.

rachel: set an automated rollback if host-ingress.p99.chat-small exceeds baseline+3% during rollout window. added canary monitors.

tomas: note: multi-frame gRPC streams still follow reassembly path; we only fast-path single-frame windows. I left reassembly unchanged.

dilip: small note on batching: for tiny routes we should bias toward fewer coalesces, more immediate submits, then rely on model-side batching to handle token-level efficiency.

rachel: agreed. let's also update docs in runtime/ingress.md to document backing_stable semantics and when kernels should set it.

observability-bot: metric tag added: kernel_affinity=stable_backing_toggle.

build-bot: canary: promoted PR 12567 to canary cluster at 2026-03-22T11:00:00Z.

tomas: local canary numbers so far: p99 down ~9% vs pre-roll, allocs -40%. will monitor for kv-hit regressions.

rachel: thanks folks. once canary is healthy we'll proceed with gradual rollout. I'll write a short postmortem note summarizing root cause and fixes.
